title: Change singular olla statements into negatives
summary: Change olen, olet, or on into en ole, et ole, or ei ole while keeping the subject and context.
objectives: Change olen, olet, or on into en ole, et ole, or ei ole while keeping the subject and context.
Apply the pattern using the supporting forms shown.

sections.title: Replace the affirmative verb
paragraphs: Change olen, olet, or on into en ole, et ole, or ei ole while keeping the subject and context.
The negative verb carries person agreement. Put the fixed form ole after it.

sections.title: Change the polarity only
paragraphs: Read the source and target meanings. Keep the subject and supplied context unchanged.
Choose the negative verb from the original subject, then add ole.

examples.finnish: Minä olen täällä. → Minä en ole täällä.
examples.english: I am here. → I am not here.

examples.finnish: Hän on valmis. → Hän ei ole valmis.
examples.english: He or she is ready. → He or she is not ready.

examples.finnish: Sinä olet kotona. → Sinä et ole kotona.
examples.english: You are at home. → You are not at home.

commonMistakes: Do not change the subject or the supplied context.
Keep ole after the person-marked negative verb.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Notice who the sentence is about. Change Hän on rauhallinen. “He or she is calm.” → ____ “He or she is not calm.” Keep the subject and context unchanged.
practiceExercises.explanation: Hän changes from on to ei ole. The negative verb carries the person ending.

Correct. Hän changes from on to ei ole. The negative verb carries the person ending.
“Me emme ole rauhallinen.” does not fit this subject or construction. Hän changes from on to ei ole. The negative verb carries the person ending.
“Hän ei on rauhallinen.” does not fit this subject or construction. Hän changes from on to ei ole. The negative verb carries the person ending.

sentenceExplanation.translation: He or she is not calm.
sentenceExplanation.pattern: subject + person-marked negative verb + ole + context

parts.role: subject: the person or people described by the sentence
parts.formation: subject pronoun; no ending is added

parts.role: negative verb: carries the person agreement
parts.formation: hän takes the negative-verb form ei

parts.role: main verb after the negative verb
parts.formation: olla uses the fixed form ole after the negative verb

parts.role: context: tells the location or state
parts.formation: supplied as a complete fixed expression; no change is required

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Change Sinä olet lääkäri. “You are a doctor.” → ____ “You are not a doctor.” Keep sinä and lääkäri unchanged.
practiceExercises.explanation: Sinä takes et; add ole and keep the subject and description unchanged.
